req.title: PUT rejects unknown player
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when PUT targets a playerId that does not exist.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-012 requires that PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} returns HTTP 404 when the targeted squad number does not exist. The endpoint uses squad_number as the natural key. Tests must cover: (1) a positive case confirming an existing player can be updated (verifying the 204 path works, so 404 is not spuriously returned), (2) a negative case confirming a completely non-existent squad number yields exactly 404, and (3) boundary cases around the edges of the known squad number space (squad number 0, squad number 27 which is one beyond the last seeded row at 26, and squad number 26 which is the last valid seeded row). The route checks retrieve_by_squad_number_async and raises HTTPException(404) when None is returned, so tests must confirm the exact status code 404 and not merely a non-2xx response. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting the exact integer 404, testing both sides of the existence boundary (26 exists, 27 does not), and verifying the positive path returns exactly 204.

tests.name: test_put_existing_player_returns_204
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 players; squad number 10 (Messi) exists
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with a valid PlayerRequestModel body where squad_number matches path
trace: R-PLAYER-012 — positive path: existing player must NOT yield 404
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

def test_put_existing_player_returns_204():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Lionel",
        "middleName": "Andrés",
        "lastName": "Messi",
        "dateOfBirth": "1987-06-24T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 10,
        "position": "Right Winger",
        "abbrPosition": "RW",
        "team": "Paris Saint-Germain",
        "league": "Ligue 1",
        "starting11": True
    }
    r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 204
    assert r.content == b""

test_put_existing_player_returns_204()

tests.name: test_put_nonexistent_squad_number_returns_404
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 players; squad number 999 does not exist
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/999 with a valid PlayerRequestModel body where squad_number=999
expected: Status code is exactly 404, not 400, not 204, not 200
trace: R-PLAYER-012 — primary error pathway: unknown playerId must yield HTTP 404
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

def test_put_nonexistent_squad_number_returns_404():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Ghost",
        "middleName": None,
        "lastName": "Player",
        "dateOfBirth": None,
        "squadNumber": 999,
        "position": "Goalkeeper",
        "abbrPosition": "GK",
        "team": None,
        "league": None,
        "starting11": False
    }
    r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/999", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 404
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 204
    assert r.status_code != 400

test_put_nonexistent_squad_number_returns_404()

tests.name: test_put_mismatch_squad_number_returns_400_not_404
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 players; squad number 10 exists
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with a body where squad_number=99 (mismatch with path)
expected: HTTP 400 Bad Request is returned (mismatch guard fires before the 404 guard)
trace: R-PLAYER-012 — DT: decision table row where squad_number body != path triggers 400 before 404 check; distinguishes 400 from 404 mutation
